362627.title: Nonexistence of spanning thin codes for prime modulus
362627.statement:

362628.title: Sullivant's saturation conjecture for Gaussian DAG models

**Sullivant's saturation conjecture.** The vanishing ideal satisfies

P_G = J_G: S_V.

363052.title: The completeness conjecture for MacMahon prime-detecting expressions
363052.statement:
Let $M_a(n)$ be the partition functions defined by

$$
M_a(n)=\sum_{\substack{0<s_1<s_2<\dots<s_a\\ n=m_1s_1+\dots+m_as_a}}m_1\cdots m_a.
$$

Let $\vec{P}(x):=(p_1(x),p_2(x),\dots,p_a(x))\in\mathbb{Z}[x]^a$ be a vector of relatively prime integer polynomials. For integers $n\geq 2$, suppose that

$$
E(n)=p_1(n)M_1(n)+p_2(n)M_2(n)+\dots+p_a(n)M_a(n)\geq 0,
$$

and that $E(n)$ vanishes precisely when $n$ is prime. **The completeness conjecture.** Then $E(n)$ is a $\mathbb{Q}[n]$-linear combination of the entries in the table of known prime-detecting expressions. This conjectures that the listed MacMahon partition-function expressions generate all prime-detecting expressions of this type; the paper presents the claim as motivated by computer evidence, with no resolution supplied.

363235.title: Regularity conjecture for t-connected ideals of trees

363542.title: The codegree isomorphism conjecture for finite simple groups
363542.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. For an irreducible character $\chi$ of $G$, define its codegree by

$$
\operatorname{cod}(\chi)=\frac{|G:\operatorname{ker}(\chi)|}{\chi(1)}.
$$

Let $\operatorname{cod}(G)$ denote the set of codegrees of irreducible characters of $G$.

**The codegree isomorphism conjecture.** Let $H$ be a finite nonabelian simple group and $G$ a finite group. Then

$$
\operatorname{cod}(G)\subseteq\operatorname{cod}(H)\quad\text{if and only if}\quad G\cong H.
$$

This is proposed as a stronger version of the codegree isomorphism conjecture, whose equality hypothesis has been confirmed for several families of simple groups. The supplied text does not give a resolution of the stronger version.

364350.title: Bayer et al.'s Betti-number conjecture for total cut complexes of grid graphs
364350.statement:

$$
b_{2n-2k}(\Delta_k^t(\mathcal{G}_{2\times n}))=\binom{n-1}{k-1},\qquad k\geq 2,
$$

and

$$
b_{3n-6}(\Delta_3^t(\mathcal{G}_{3\times n}))=\binom{2n-2}{2}.
$$

The conjecture predicts the nonzero Betti numbers of total cut complexes for two families of grid graphs. It was subsequently confirmed by homotopy-equivalence results giving wedges of spheres with the indicated multiplicities and dimensions.

364371.title: The top elementary coefficient conjecture for Segre powers of Boolean lattices
364371.statement:
Let $B_n^{(t)}$ denote the $t$-fold Segre power of the Boolean lattice, and let $\tilde{H}_{n-2}(B_n^{(t)})$ be its reduced homology with the induced $\mathfrak{S}_n$-action. Write its Frobenius characteristic in the elementary symmetric-function basis:

$$
\operatorname{ch}\,\tilde{H}_{n-2}(B_n^{(t)})=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}a_\lambda e_\lambda.
$$

**Top elementary coefficient conjecture.** The coefficient of $e_n$ is always $1$, that is, $a_{(n)}=1$.

This conjecture concerns the diagonal $\mathfrak{S}_n$-action on the homology of Segre powers of Boolean lattices. The paper reports that Sage computations for $n,t\leqslant7$ support it; its general validity remains open.

364372.title: Irreducible-support stability conjecture for Segre powers of Boolean lattices
364372.statement:
Let $B_n^{(t)}$ denote the $t$-fold Segre power of the Boolean lattice, and let $\tilde{H}_{n-2}(B_n^{(t)})$ be its reduced homology representation of $\mathfrak{S}_n$. An irreducible $\mathfrak{S}_n$-representation **appears** in $\tilde{H}_{n-2}(B_n^{(t)})$ when it occurs as a constituent of that representation.

**Irreducible-support stability conjecture.** For $t\geqslant3$, every irreducible appearing in $\tilde{H}_{n-2}(B_n^{(t)})$ also appears in $\tilde{H}_{n-2}(B_n^{(2)})$.

364480.title: Odd-part dominance for elementary symmetric products of partition parts
364480.statement:
For a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_\ell)$, let $\operatorname{pre}_i(\lambda)$ be the partition whose parts are all products $\lambda_{i_1}\cdots\lambda_{i_i}$ with $1\leq i_1<\cdots<i_i\leq\ell$, and set $\operatorname{pre}_i(\lambda)=\emptyset$ when $\ell<i$. Let $o_i(n)$ be the number of partitions in $\operatorname{pre}_i(\mathcal P(n))$ with odd parts, and let $d_i(n)$ be the number with distinct parts. **Odd-part dominance conjecture.**

$$
o_2(n)\geq d_2(n)\quad(n\geq0),\qquad o_3(n)\geq d_3(n)\quad(n\geq21).
$$

These inequalities are based on numerical evidence and relate the parity and distinctness of partitions formed from elementary symmetric products; the source does not establish them.

record.title: Leander's generalized Helleseth conjecture for permutations
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a finite field, let $L^\times$ be its multiplicative group, and let $f\colon L\to L$ be a permutation. For each $\lambda\in L^\times$, write $(\lambda f)(x)=\lambda f(x)$ and define

$$
\mathfrak D(\lambda f)=\prod_{a\in L^\times}\widehat{\lambda f}(a),
$$

where

$$
\widehat{\lambda f}(a)=\sum_{x\in L}\mu(ax+\lambda f(x)).
$$

**Leander's generalized Helleseth conjecture.** If $f$ is a permutation of $L$, then

$$
\prod_{\lambda\in L^\times}\mathfrak D(\lambda f)=0.
$$

record.title: Peng–Zhao's clique conjecture for dense uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $t$, $m$, and $r\geq 3$ be positive integers satisfying

$$

**Peng–Zhao's conjecture.** The Lagrangian of $G$ satisfies

$$
\lambda(G)=\lambda([t-1]^{(r)}).
$$

This conjecture concerns the extremal Lagrangian of an $r$-uniform hypergraph in the range where its number of edges is between that of the complete $r$-graph on $t-1$ vertices and that quantity plus ${t-2 \choose r-1}$. record.title: The reduced-graph order conjecture of Akbari, Cameron, and Khosrovshahi
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$, and let a **reduced graph** mean a graph with no pair of vertices that can be removed without changing the relevant adjacency-matrix rank. Write $m(r)$ for

$$
m(r)=\begin{cases}2^{(r+2)/2}-2&\text{if }r\text{ is even},\\5\cdot2^{(r-3)/2}-2&\text{if }r\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$
 **Akbari–Cameron–Khosrovshahi conjecture.** The order of any reduced graph of rank $r$ is at most $m(r)$. This conjecture is presented as a bound on the order of reduced graphs in terms of adjacency-matrix rank; the paper cites it as a proposal of Akbari, Cameron, and Khosrovshahi, without giving a resolution.

record.title: Equality of the hybrid Floer–Morse and holomorphic curve-counting maps
record.statement:
Let $C$ be the underlying curve, let $\Sigma$ be a real exact Lagrangian in $T^*C$, and let $q_1,\dots,q_\kappa$ be points of $C$. The maps

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{hol}}\colon HW(\sqcup_{i=1}^\kappa T^*_{q_i}C)\to \operatorname{Mat}(N^{\kappa},\operatorname{BSk}_\kappa(\Sigma))
$$

and

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{Mor}}\colon HW(\sqcup_{i=1}^\kappa T^*_{q_i}C)\to \operatorname{Mat}(N^{\kappa},\operatorname{BSk}_\kappa(\Sigma))
$$

are respectively defined by holomorphic curve counts and by counting holomorphic curves coupled with folded Morse flow trees. **Equality of the hybrid Floer–Morse and holomorphic curve-counting maps.**

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{Mor}}=\mathcal{F}_{\operatorname{hol}}.
$$

This identifies the hybrid Floer–Morse construction with the holomorphic curve-counting construction and is intended to make the connection with the spectral network associated to the spectral curve more transparent. record.title: The perfect Prishchepov group type conjecture
record.statement:
Let $P(r,n,k,s,q)$ denote the Prishchepov group with parameters $r,n,k,s,q$, and let a group be **perfect** when its abelianization is trivial. A group is of type $\widetilde{\mathfrak{Z}}$ when it satisfies the type $\widetilde{\mathfrak{Z}}$ condition defined for Prishchepov groups. Let $n,k,q \geq 1$ and $2 \leq r<n$ with

$$
\gcd(n,k-1,q)=1.
$$

Suppose

$$
k\not\equiv 1 \pmod{n}\qquad\text{and}\qquad k\not\equiv 1+q \pmod{n}.
$$

**The perfect Prishchepov group type conjecture.** If $P(r,n,k,r-1,q)$ is perfect, then it is of type $\widetilde{\mathfrak{Z}}$. This conjecture predicts that every perfect nontrivial group in this parameter range has the indicated structural type. The claim is motivated by the fact that all known perfect nontrivial examples satisfying the hypotheses have this type; its general validity remains open.

record.title: Hecke-word Euler characteristic conjecture for transmission loci
record.statement:
Let $\widetilde{\Sigma}_k$ be the relevant set of transmission permutations, and let $\tau\in\widetilde{\Sigma}_k$ have shift $0$ and satisfy $\operatorname{inv}_k(\tau)\leq g$. Let $(C,p,q)$ be a general point of $\cM_{g,2}$ if $k=0$, or of $\cH_{g,k,2}$ if $k\geq 2$. A length-$g$ Hecke word for $\tau$ is a factorization

$$
\tau=\alpha_1\star\alpha_2\star\cdots\star\alpha_g
$$

where each $\alpha_i$ has shift $0$ and $\operatorname{inv}_k(\alpha_i)\leq 1$; equivalently, each $\alpha_i$ is either $\operatorname{id}$ or $\sigma^k_m$ for some $m\in\mathbb Z$. Let $H^\tau_g$ be the set of length-$g$ Hecke words for $\tau$.

**Hecke-word Euler characteristic conjecture.**

$$
\chi\left(W^\tau(C,p,q),\mathcal O_{W^\tau(C,p,q)}\right)=(-1)^{g-\operatorname{inv}_k(\tau)}\#H^\tau_g.
$$

The source motivates this as a generalization of the Euler-characteristic formula for Brill–Noether varieties and notes that better information on relative transmission loci, especially flatness criteria, is needed to prove it.

record.title: Esperet et al.'s flow reconfiguration equivalence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and $k$ a positive integer. A **$k$-flow** is a nowhere-zero integer flow with $0<|f(e)|<k$ on every edge, and an **$A$-flow** is a nowhere-zero flow with values in an abelian group $A$. **Esperet et al.'s flow reconfiguration conjecture.** For each graph $G$ and each positive integer $k$,

$$
\mathcal{F}(G,k)\text{ is connected if and only if }\mathcal{F}(G,\mathbb{Z}_k)\text{ is connected}.
$$

One direction is easy, since reducing flow values modulo $k$ maps walks to walks. The reverse direction remains open; the source also gives examples showing that reconfiguration can distinguish nonisomorphic groups of the same order.

340900.title: Conjecture on perfect linear hypergraphs and disjoint unions
340900.statement:
Let $r\ge 3$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph is **linear** if any two edges have at most $1$ vertex in common, and an $r$-uniform hypergraph is **perfect** if its Lagrangian density equals that of the complete $r$-graph on one fewer vertex. For $r$-graphs $G$ and $H$, let $G\bigsqcup H$ denote their disjoint union.

**Perfectness conjecture.** (1) For $r\ge 3$, there exists $n$ such that every linear $r$-uniform hypergraph with at least $n$ vertices is perfect. (2) For $r\ge 3$, there exists $n$ such that if $G$ and $H$ are perfect $r$-graphs with at least $n$ vertices, then $G\bigsqcup H$ is perfect.

The conjecture proposes broad classes of perfect hypergraphs, extending the fact that all $2$-graphs are perfect and that most hypergraphs with known Lagrangian densities are perfect. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.

375665.title: Aydinian–Blinovsky refinement of the MMS conjecture
375665.statement:
Let $n\ge 2$ be an integer. Let $\mathcal{N}_n$ be the family of multisets $P=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$ of real numbers satisfying $\sum_{j=1}^n x_j=0$. Choose $\mathbb{I}\in\binom{[n]}{k}$ uniformly at random and define

$$
X_P=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{I}}x_j.
$$

For $i\in[n-1]$, let $H_i\sim\operatorname{Hyp}(n,i,k)$ be a hypergeometric random variable.

**Aydinian–Blinovsky refinement.** For every $k\in[n-1]$ and every $P\in\mathcal{N}_n$,

$$
\mathbb{P}(X_P\ge 0)\ge\min_{i\in[n-1]}\mathbb{P}\left(H_i\ge\frac{ik}{n}\right).
$$

This refines the MMS conjecture and is stated to cover all non-trivial parameter instances. The source gives no resolution status for the refinement, so it is recorded as open.

332003.title: Flip-length bound by the maximum rotation length in dihedral groups
332003.literal:
Let $D_n$ be a dihedral group, let $S$ be a generating set, and let $l_S(g)$ denote the length of an element $g$ with respect to $S$. For an integer $m$ with $0<m<n$, consider the element $r^m f$. **Flip-length bound.** We conjecture that

$$
l_S(r^m f) \leq \max_{0 \leq k < n}\{l_S(r^k)\}.
$$

This conjecture follows the observation that bounds for powers of $r$ can be transferred to flips by expressing $r^m f$ using suitable generators. Its truth is stated not to affect the results of the lemmas that follow.

328829.title: Generalized structured-cover conjecture for multipartite hypergraphs
328829.literal:
Let $H$ be an $r$-partite hypergraph with matching number $

$$
\bigcup_{i\leqslant k}S_i
$$

is a cover of $H$.

This would generalize the preceding structured-cover assertion and imply a strengthened form of Ryser's conjecture. The paper presents it as open.

328955.title: The quotient-of-sumsets small-doubling conjecture
328955.literal:
Let $A\subset\mathbb C$ be a finite set, and write

$$
\frac{A+A}{A+A}=\left\{\frac{x}{y}:x,y\in A+A,\ y\ne 0\right\}.
$$

**Quotient-of-sumsets small-doubling conjecture.** There exist absolute constants $c$ and $c'$ such that

$$
\left|\frac{A+A}{A+A}\right|\leq c|A|^2\ \Rightarrow\ |A+A|\leq c'|A|.
$$

The conjecture asks whether near-extremality of the quotient-of-sumsets bound forces $A$ to have small sumset. The paper proves weaker bounds in this direction and notes analogous conjectures for $(A-A)/(A-A)$, $A(A+A+A+A)$, and $(A-A)(A-A)$; the conjecture itself is presented as open.

329136.title: Christofides–Markström conjecture on the fractional clique-cover bound
329136.literal:
